Keeping raw occurrences here leaves those decisions possible later.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 5.8 A fact is saved only if everything its decision relied on still holds at that moment: the check and the write happen together, protected against conflicting changes (plain code). If a relevant change invalidates the approved save, nothing is saved and the assigned job is held (8.14). A test run uses the same checks.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Immutable history, compatible blank filling, snapshot conflicts, exact replays, logged allowed field changes, no deletion/rekey, new amendment events and atomic check/write are storage/read operations. Keeping raw occurrences here leaves those decisions possible later.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 3.11 Optional links to XBRL data (§6): at most one official line item (metric facts only; the same one named in `xbrl_qname`), and any number of breakdown members (any fact type), each saying which slice part it supports.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Optional official-data links do not filter discovery; exact cardinalities and slice support are checked when linking.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.1 Attach the exact company-reported line item, or attach nothing. A wrong link does silent damage that nothing undoes after saving (6.18); a missing link fills itself in on a later run at no risk.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Choose exact company line-item link or no link; reader creates neither.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.2 Only a base metric gets a direct link. Guidance and surprise facts inherit the line-item link of the metric Driver named by their base (1.18), only when that Driver has facts for the same subject company public before the read's date; actions never link; a non-GAAP measurement blocks inheritance. *Why:* a forecast or surprise has no XBRL line of its own; the line lives on the metric. Otherwise they get no link for now; a direct guidance or surprise link is never written to fill the gap.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Base-only links/inheritance, GAAP-compatible tags, excluded classes, exact metric identity and refusal-only structural checks govern links. These cannot become discovery exclusions.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.3 A fact's measurement tags count as GAAP-compatible only when they are empty or exactly one of `gaap`, `basic`, `diluted`, `reported`, `as_reported`. Anything else, including any combination, → no link.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Base-only links/inheritance, GAAP-compatible tags, excluded classes, exact metric identity and refusal-only structural checks govern links. These cannot become discovery exclusions.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.4 Never linked, as a principle and not a word list: events and macro causes (resignation, buyback, oil price, interest rates, tariffs, weather…); ratios, derived and growth figures (margins, growth, return on invested capital, EBITDA, free cash flow, per-square-foot, mix…); non-GAAP or adjusted figures. Tax rates are real GAAP line items and may link.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Base-only links/inheritance, GAAP-compatible tags, excluded classes, exact metric identity and refusal-only structural checks govern links. These cannot become discovery exclusions.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.5 A match must be the same metric: cost of revenue ≠ revenue, a subtotal ≠ its total, basic ≠ diluted. Refuse anything related-but-different: GAAP vs non-GAAP, gross vs net, subtotal vs total, the wrong statement, or a breakdown instead of the consolidated line. When two candidates are equally good, take the more widely used one. When unsure, refuse.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Base-only links/inheritance, GAAP-compatible tags, excluded classes, exact metric identity and refusal-only structural checks govern links. These cannot become discovery exclusions.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.6 Fixed checks, which can only refuse a link, never create one:
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Base-only links/inheritance, GAAP-compatible tags, excluded classes, exact metric identity and refusal-only structural checks govern links. These cannot become discovery exclusions.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.7 The candidates are the company's own consolidated numeric line items, cut at the fact's public time for history (live may use the latest). The chosen item must be exactly on that list. Only 10-K and 10-Q filings (and their amendments) carry XBRL; 8-Ks never do.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Company/date-cut line-item menus and supported filing types are link preparation; no historical evidence is borrowed into discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.8 A line item missing from the database never blocks the fact; the link fills in later.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Missing line item does not block discovery. Later filling of the optional link is outside the prompt.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.9 A link to a breakdown member needs both its axis and its member. It's valid only when it matches one real tagged fact exactly: the subject company, line item, duration or instant, exact dates, and the complete set of breakdowns (including "none"). Two different breakdown sets are never combined; that would invent a combination no filing has.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Exact axis/member sets, dates, subject and explicit consolidated context are source/link validation, not a prose reader’s final judgment.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.10 When a source supplies XBRL data, it always includes the exact reporting context (the dates, and whether the value covers a span or a single moment); every breakdown carries both axis and member; and "no breakdowns" is sent only as an explicit, checked statement. A missed extraction must never pass as the consolidated whole.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Exact axis/member sets, dates, subject and explicit consolidated context are source/link validation, not a prose reader’s final judgment.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.11 Only text can create Drivers or non-metric facts. Tagged filing data never decides meaning or identity; it may add numeric metric facts only after the Driver and the company's link to that line item are already admitted, and that route is switched off for now (6.12).
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Text remains discovery baseline. Admitted tagged metric additions, proofs, exact numeric handling and text/tag reconciliation require their separate full design; target ON does not authorize bypassing proofs.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 6.12 **Facts from tagged filing data:** an approved design, switched off until its proofs pass; its full rules are in folded Part A1.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Text remains discovery baseline. Admitted tagged metric additions, proofs, exact numeric handling and text/tag reconciliation require their separate full design; target ON does not authorize bypassing proofs.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.1 Two facts belong to the same series (one continuous history line) only if all of these match exactly: company, Driver, fact type, slice, resolved period, period kind, measurement tags, series unit, time type and, for surprises, the surprise kind. Family is added only for cross-flavor views: joined by name (1.18) and across synonym links if any exist (1.19, 6.20), only between facts that match on everything else above, and using only facts public before the view's date (1.14). A guidance or surprise Driver's own facts are always readable on their own.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Exact-series grouping and unknown-unit isolation concern stored facts and as-of reads.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.2 Series units group by exact equality: no unit families, and `unknown` is never absorbed. Facts with an `unknown` series unit stay readable on their own; they are never grouped into a comparable series, not even with each other.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Exact-series grouping and unknown-unit isolation concern stored facts and as-of reads.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.3 Within one event: combine pieces before settling conflicts (5.2). Clean stated parts beat a vague `mixed` fact. A whole-company fact exists only when it is itself stated.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: No unstated company total is discovered. Compatible piece fusion, conflict order and clean-part preference happen later.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.4 Display order: value → signed change → comparison → guidance words → the trimmed quote (last resort). Duplicates are judged by the stated value or range and its unit, or by the tidied guidance words for qualitative facts; never by the quote; facts protected by 5.9 are never collapsed. A citation is the Driver name, plus the scope when needed.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Display priorities, citation formatting and protected occurrence deduplication are read operations.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.5 Same company, series and day: rank `8k` > `transcript` > `10q` > `10k` > `news`; then the later timestamp, then the source ID. Across days, the latest is the current view and earlier facts stay as history. "Day" means US Eastern time. The same number stated in different sources (e.g. an 8-K, then a 10-Q) is stored as separate facts on separate events; only reads pick one.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Separate source events remain separate evidence. Source/day ordering, Eastern day, timestamp/ID ties and latest views are downstream.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.6 History reads use strictly "before the as-of date"; live reads see the current data. Predictions and historical explanations follow A2.5.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Caller/view historical time cutoffs, not quote discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.8 A direction plus basis points or percentage points, without "to X", is a change, not a level (3.50). "Narrowed" is worked out when read from consecutive closed ranges, never stored.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Change-versus-level representation, narrowed ranges, exact-member grouping, raw/reconciled labels and required views happen after fact construction/storage.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.9 Labels are grouped by XBRL member only within one company and slice part, only when they share one exact axis-and-member pair, and only when each label has at least one linked fact and all their linked facts agree. A conflict is logged as a warning and the system carries on; it never waits for a person. Facts without links follow their own label. The group is keyed by the pair, not a label, and only the display grouping changes.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Change-versus-level representation, narrowed ranges, exact-member grouping, raw/reconciled labels and required views happen after fact construction/storage.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.10 Every read result is labeled `raw` or `reconciled`, and a reconciled result is returned only when asked for. Reconciled views arrive with company renames in release 2 (9.10); they can be switched off, and use only time-aware rename links (6.13–6.16): followed hop by hop, public before the as-of date, with no model calls. Rename chains are the only reconciled view. A second view (grouping by unknown XBRL axis) was reviewed and deferred; don't rebuild it without a fresh owner decision.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Change-versus-level representation, narrowed ranges, exact-member grouping, raw/reconciled labels and required views happen after fact construction/storage.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 7.11 **Views the reads must offer:** raw (every stored fact, unchanged); current (the winning fact per series, with conflicts still visible); history (earlier facts before a cutoff); point-in-time (any of these, using only what was public before a given time); reconciled (7.10, from release 2); and cross-company or industry comparisons (the same Driver, with companies grouped by the official industry data as of that time, 2.42). Every program reads facts only through these views, never straight from storage. *Why:* then how facts are read changes in one place.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Change-versus-level representation, narrowed ranges, exact-member grouping, raw/reconciled labels and required views happen after fact construction/storage.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.4 **Guidance movement: stored when stated, otherwise worked out when read.**
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Forecast statements survive discovery. Stated/unstated movement, midpoint/read-time rules, source corrections and forecasted-change versus revision fields are later, never guessed here.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.5 A correction with no business-change wording (known from the source's details or explicit correction wording) gets its worked-out guidance movement forced to `unknown`, so a typo fix is never read as a raise or a cut.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Forecast statements survive discovery. Stated/unstated movement, midpoint/read-time rules, source corrections and forecasted-change versus revision fields are later, never guessed here.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.6 **Guidance amounts: value or revision?** Percent-only guidance stores its growth basis in `level_unit`. On a guidance fact, a change is only the forecast's own revision ("we raised our cost forecast by $4B"); a forecast that the measure itself will change ("we expect costs to rise by more than $4B") is the forecast's value, with the word that says it is a change kept as a tag (3.26). It is neither a revision nor a forecast of the total.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Forecast statements survive discovery. Stated/unstated movement, midpoint/read-time rules, source corrections and forecasted-change versus revision fields are later, never guessed here.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.7 `value_text`: a forecast in words, for guidance facts with no numbers only. Tidied, at most 200 characters, with no stored numbers (the number fields stay empty); date and period anchors are allowed.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Numberless forecasts and exact conditions survive. The 200-character value_text format, guidance-only slots, numeric exclusions and assumptions-versus-cause field split are later representation work.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.8 `conditions`: guidance only, and assumptions only, never causes (3.53); the condition's wording must remain in the quote.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Numberless forecasts and exact conditions survive. The 200-character value_text format, guidance-only slots, numeric exclusions and assumptions-versus-cause field split are later representation work.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.9 `company_confirmed`: `true` means the company or its management stated or confirmed it. It's required on every stored guidance fact and decided from who-said-it evidence; sources supply only the evidence. Unclear who said it → the fact is skipped. For now, third-party or rumored guidance is never stored as company guidance, so `false` is never used (9.2). A later company confirmation is a new fact at its own public time; history is never rewritten. *Why only on guidance:* it is the only type whose states can't say "rumored".
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Authorship/confirmation evidence and unclear-author skip are explicit. Final company_confirmed values, pending third-party representation and later-confirmation history are not decided here.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.18 A withdrawal spreads to other forecasts only when **all** of these hold:
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Find source withdrawal/reaffirmation/retraction wording; do not expand. Exact Driver/period/slice, open covered history, per-forecast replacements, late coverage, read deduplication and exact-scope numberless retractions require later history and unresolved owner design.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.19 A covered forecast that the same source replaces, reaffirms or keeps is not withdrawn; it gets its own new fact. That exclusion is per forecast; the other covered forecasts are still withdrawn.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Find source withdrawal/reaffirmation/retraction wording; do not expand. Exact Driver/period/slice, open covered history, per-forecast replacements, late coverage, read deduplication and exact-scope numberless retractions require later history and unresolved owner design.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.20 Add only, never delete. An older covered forecast that arrives late gets its missing `withdrawn` fact under the same conditions. Repeat withdrawals of an already-withdrawn forecast are ignored when read.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Find source withdrawal/reaffirmation/retraction wording; do not expand. Exact Driver/period/slice, open covered history, per-forecast replacements, late coverage, read deduplication and exact-scope numberless retractions require later history and unresolved owner design.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.21 A retraction with no replacement becomes a numberless fact (for guidance: `withdrawn`) only when the Driver and scope are exact. If they're not exact, don't guess.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Find source withdrawal/reaffirmation/retraction wording; do not expand. Exact Driver/period/slice, open covered history, per-forecast replacements, late coverage, read deduplication and exact-scope numberless retractions require later history and unresolved owner design.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 9.2 **Only company-confirmed guidance** is stored (4.9). Third-party or rumored guidance-like claims are never stored as company guidance. Allowing them later needs its own design (separate reads, ranking, comparison, later-confirmation history, source attribution and user-facing behavior), so they can never pass as company guidance. The action state `rumored` is a separate rule and unaffected.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Do not label third-party reporting as company confirmation. Target everything-ON does not supply the missing separate history/ranking/attribution schema; retain raw source evidence, do not invent storage rules.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 9.11 **No outside forecasts yet (`expectation`, 1.22).** They are skipped. Switching on needs its own design; draft fields: the forecasting firm (not the outlet reporting it), the analyst, the date it was set and the period it's for, plus the usual fact fields. Earlier text can then be backfilled from the saved originals (1.17).
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Outside forecast discovery is ON by the opening directive. Draft forecasting-firm/analyst/date/period fields are preserved as source wording, not converted into an unapproved final schema.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 9.8 **No text values on metrics, no conditions on actions.** Text values on metrics are reconsidered only if a count of real metric facts shows both many numberless readings and real changes the stored states missed (and then only in the source's exact words); conditions on actions only if a count shows that real caveats are common.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Qualitative metrics and action caveats remain in exact quotes. The target activation does not specify new metric text/action-condition storage slots or waive their evidence/design conditions; discovery invents none.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.1 **What goes where:**
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Find both surprise and companion and retain exact comparison kinds. Final kind/baseline/period fields and own-guide movement representation are assigned later.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.2 The three kinds of surprise comparison: `actual_vs_consensus` · `actual_vs_guidance` · `guidance_vs_consensus`. One surprise Driver holds all three; the kind is part of the fact's scope (3.2).
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Find both surprise and companion and retain exact comparison kinds. Final kind/baseline/period fields and own-guide movement representation are assigned later.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.3 The surprise kind comes from the basis (a result or a forecast) combined with the baseline (consensus or the company's earlier guidance). Never infer the basis from whether a period has ended.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Find both surprise and companion and retain exact comparison kinds. Final kind/baseline/period fields and own-guide movement representation are assigned later.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.10 **Surprise, when it's `in_line`:** whenever there are no words saying good or bad, and the compared value (a result or a forecast) sits inside a closed expectation range or exactly on its edge. This includes a forecast range that contains the consensus number. A beat or miss with no such words that lands strictly inside a closed range is corrected to `in_line`. A value at a stated floor or ceiling is `in_line`.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Range overlap/edge, good/bad wording, direction meaning, forbidden stock-reaction/sign shortcuts and unknown outcomes determine beat/missed/in_line fields later. Discovery retains the whole comparison phrase.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.11 **Surprise, when it's `beat` or `missed`:** a judgment of the whole phrase, aware of negation, direction and scope. Never assume higher is better, and never map "above" to beat. Words like "above", "below", "exceeded", "ahead of" or "beat the budget" never count as good or bad on their own; they take the same test. An actual range that overlaps the expectation unclearly → `unknown`, unless the source says good or bad.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Range overlap/edge, good/bad wording, direction meaning, forbidden stock-reaction/sign shortcuts and unknown outcomes determine beat/missed/in_line fields later. Discovery retains the whole comparison phrase.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.12 A result outside the range with no good/bad words needs a stated basis for which direction is good: either the source's own framing, or the metric's meaning. The metric's normal meaning (e.g. more revenue is good) may be used only when there's no common opposite story; capex, R&D, inventory, hiring and cash burn always have one, so they need the source's own framing. Circular, market-reaction, strategy-guess or single-keyword reasons don't count. No valid basis → `unknown`.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Range overlap/edge, good/bad wording, direction meaning, forbidden stock-reaction/sign shortcuts and unknown outcomes determine beat/missed/in_line fields later. Discovery retains the whole comparison phrase.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.13 Good or bad (beat or miss) is never assigned from the sign of a number; meaning decides.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Range overlap/edge, good/bad wording, direction meaning, forbidden stock-reaction/sign shortcuts and unknown outcomes determine beat/missed/in_line fields later. Discovery retains the whole comparison phrase.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.14 Every grounded surprise (one tied to a specific metric or forecast, unlike a generic "results beat") needs a matching home fact in the same event: a result surprise → its metric fact; a `guidance_vs_consensus` surprise → its guidance fact. They must match on subject company, family, period, period kind, slice, measurement and, when there are values, the tidied value and unit. A numberless surprise needs a numberless home. The home fact must itself be accepted for writing; a held or rejected home doesn't count. The home fact must belong to the surprise's family by name: for a result surprise, the metric Driver of its base (born in the same save if new); for `guidance_vs_consensus`, the guidance Driver of its base (no metric Driver needed).
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Reader finds the source-stated surprise and matching evidence. Named-family equality, exact normalized fields and final accepted-home requirement are mandatory downstream; a candidate home does not authorize a write.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.15 An ungrounded "results beat" is held. A result surprise before its period has ended is rejected. A missing home fact means the whole event is read again, never just the surprise alone.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Reader flags generic or premature surprises and missing companion rereads. Caller enforces whole-job retries and resolves the unspecified-trigger hold tension with 8.15; no endless loop is authorized.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.16 When a source states several comparisons, the home fact keeps exactly one main baseline (e.g. the prior-year headline). An expectation comparison stated alongside is never added to the home fact. The reader must spot it in the source itself (never from an already-stored comparison) and record it as its own surprise fact, where the expectation is stored.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Reader finds every expectation comparison directly from the source. Exactly one main non-expectation baseline on the home and expectation fields on the surprise are later field assignments.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 4.17 On a surprise, the change is usually empty because it can be worked out from the two values. It is stored only when the source states a difference that can't be worked out and its sign is clear. "Beat by X" with an unclear sign stays empty (the quote carries it). Otherwise it's worked out when read as result − expectation, with good or bad applied at that point.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Store only permitted explicit differences with clear sign; calculate allowed result-minus-expectation at read time. Raw discovery does not compute a difference.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 1.3 The loop it serves: extract facts → explain price moves → learn which Drivers matter → predict → trade. *Why not just list events:* services like RavenPack only list that an event happened; this system grades each cause against what the stock actually did.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Overall explain/learn/predict/trade loop; not a source-reader instruction.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 1.4 Drivers come from earnings reports (8-Ks, transcripts), news (mostly macro, sector or industry) and fiscal.ai data (10-K, 10-Q, presentations). The earnings predictor only *reads* Driver tags, to find relevant past reports and to know what moves prices; it never creates Drivers.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Source channels and predictor read-only restriction are caller/system responsibilities.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 1.20 Covered companies are those the official company → industry → sector data marks eligible at one recorded moment. The resulting count is an outcome, never a target (no fixed 786 or 796).
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Official eligibility snapshots, catalog refresh and preserved histories are caller/catalog policy, not candidate-text classification.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 1.21 A newly eligible company may get facts right away and joins the catalog at the next reviewed refresh. A company that stops being eligible adds nothing new to the catalog, but all its facts and history stay intact and readable. Nothing is deleted, renamed, merged or rewritten automatically. An unclear status keeps history and blocks new catalog inclusion; it never creates a company-specific exception or a second lifecycle list.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Official eligibility snapshots, catalog refresh and preserved histories are caller/catalog policy, not candidate-text classification.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.8 Quotes are exact source text, found in the source. AI never rewrites, repairs or swaps a quote.

- 8.9 **What a source may send.** A source sends only evidence, as stated. It must never send what the core decides: Driver names, fact IDs or scope, a fiscal year or quarter it worked out, measurement tags, final units, or any number it calculated. The approved rule is to reject the whole item if it does; it replaces an older rule (ignore such fields and recompute them) once proven.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Before reading, reject the whole source item if its sender supplied core-decided names/fact IDs/scope/derived fiscal values/tags/final units/calculated numbers, subject to the rule’s proof gate. Numbered extraction unit IDs are locators, not fact IDs. Do not silently drop bad fields and salvage an invalid item.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.10 **The AI reader covers the whole source event**, in order, across as many reads as needed; each read fits its limit and carries the context its text refers to. Nothing is shortened, skipped or counted as read without being read.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: The prompt requires complete ordered reads with needed context. Caller manages token limits, multiple reads, manifests and evidence access; the prompt cannot repair missing or unavailable original material.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.11 Old Guidance data is evidence only: it is never converted, replayed or bridged into Driver facts, and never used to fill a history gap. Whether to accept a measured temporary history gap or wait for fresh Driver history is decided only when the old data is retired. A read with no Driver facts returns an empty result, never old Guidance data. Retiring the old Guidance system keeps a complete, restorable copy; only explicitly approved parts are removed.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: No replay/bridge of old Guidance into candidates. Retention/removal and temporary gap decisions belong to retirement/read planning.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 9.4 **No 8-K item-number categories.** An 8-K's item number is information only. It may not create, merge, type, rank or route a Driver or fact. Reopen only for a named user with a testable need, and never with a hand-written item map, a meaning shortcut or a second reader.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Item numbers cannot decide meaning here; no hand-written item map or second reader is added. Activation/routing design remains caller work.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 9.5 **Target sources:** Reports, Transcripts and News; every channel must pass its certification before activation. The starting source/channel set and ongoing coverage remain to be agreed (10.1); other source formats are not automatically admitted. News saving, ticker links, edits, return updates, readers and activation prerequisites follow [NewsMultipleSymbols.md](NewsMultipleSymbols.md). Selected original research articles may be saved without tracked tickers; new ordinary feed stories without tracked tickers remain skipped. Research-found filings/calls retain their Report/Transcript types.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Prompt accepts the specified source types only. Actual starting coverage, channel certification and News activation/link/version prerequisites remain before production.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 1.14 **No look-ahead.** A historical run may see only facts that were public before its cutoff (historical explanations: A2.5); names follow today's catalog (see below).
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Caller withholds disallowed context and applies public-time cutoffs; catalog matching, targeted-history exception, slice/XBRL candidate cutoffs and live trading evaluation are separate. Reader-specific isolation is explicit in the prompt.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 1.25 **A prediction never sees the outcome it predicts, even inside a source's own text** (e.g. a story that reports the price move). Adds to 1.14.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: This task produces candidates, not predictions. Owner clarified that fact producers exclude system-calculated returns, while returns stated in the document remain readable. Prediction-side exclusion of the outcome being predicted is a separate rule, not widened into a source-reading ban here.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.14 **Every item ends in one of five recorded outcomes.** Nothing disappears silently.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Reader candidates-or-one-reason and complete-search conditions are explicit. Written/merged/held/skipped/rejected records, split-company keys, atomic job failure and rejection precedence require a caller/writer, not the draft reader schema.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.15 **A held item is retried only when a specific, checkable event could change the result.**
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Incomplete search is not final not-found. Exact checkable triggers, source-unavailability-only general retry, final valid refusal, later-source-as-own-event, exact reopening and whole-job context are caller duties. Generic/artifact holds lack a named trigger in the specific clauses; report this gap rather than invent one.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.16 **Running rules already decided:**
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Own-source/no-price-gate discovery is included. New metric history oldest first, daily move research, initial/update workflows, at-most-one find-aid Driver, time-correct late sources and measured live/history capacity are orchestration. This prompt is new discovery, not the optional named-driver targeted search mode.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 10.3 **Service targets:** how fast new facts must appear, expected volumes, schedules, alerts and budgets were never set. The running rules that are decided are in 1.14, 8.15 and 8.16. *Affects:* running the system. *Decide when:* you plan how it runs.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Service targets, volume, schedules, alerts and budgets are not source-prompt instructions.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.12 AI calls run on subscriptions only: no API billing, no switching providers, no silent fallback. Any pay-per-use service, such as paid embeddings used only to *suggest* match candidates (never to decide), needs its own separate owner approval.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Subscription-only authorization, no fallback/provider switching, fixed bounded technical retries, attempt logs and no rerolling valid no/unsure decisions are orchestration rules. No AI test calls are run in this review.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.13 Passing a test qualifies an AI only for that exact task, model, program running it, connection and configuration, and kind of input; it never carries over.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Exact task/model/program/connection/configuration/input-specific certification, not automatically transferable to this draft.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.17 **Quality bar: fewer than 1% wrong, measured at launch.** A fact is wrong if any material claim in it is incorrect or unsupported by its own source; it counts once, however many parts are wrong. Nothing after saving finds or fixes mistakes (6.20), so the checks before saving must meet this bar on their own.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Fewer-than-1% measured launch error, fresh fixed answer-key tests, qualified independent graders, honest upper bounds, miss/refusal counts and meaning-based grading remain required. A coverage map or matching quote is not proof of model accuracy or recall.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 8.18 Judge accuracy on meaning, never by checking that text matches. *Why:* on the same data, quote-matching looked ~99% right while judged accuracy was ~29%.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Fewer-than-1% measured launch error, fresh fixed answer-key tests, qualified independent graders, honest upper bounds, miss/refusal counts and meaning-based grading remain required. A coverage map or matching quote is not proof of model accuracy or recall.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 9.7 **Daily price explanations are in this target version.** AI supplies judgments and code validates/saves them under A2.1–A2.8. Approval of this design does not certify or activate a producer.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: No unsolicited classification field is added; daily explanation design is independent of candidate extraction. Target override does not invent missing field design or certify a producer.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - 10.1 **Still to choose:** significant-move benchmarks, thresholds and measured intervals, including moves without a source; starting/ongoing source coverage, history limits and research budgets. Before returns drive triggers or trading evaluation, complete [EXPLAINED_BY.md §8](EXPLAINED_BY.md#8-return-measurements--open-checks-for-the-next-bot) or exclude unverified measurements. Missing/unusable returns remain unknown, never zero. *Affects:* source coverage, deeper research and return-based evaluation. *Decide when:* before each is enabled.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Coverage, history/research budgets and verified return-based triggers remain owner choices; source reader never needs a price move to retain a fact.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - A2.1 The shared update process uses AI to judge which source-backed facts contributed to an observed move and why (8.16). Code validates the fact/source references, existing affected Company ID, trading Date and required fields, then saves through the existing shared validation/writing path. Timestamps alone never prove causation. A producer does not copy the core's validation or writing steps.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Judgments, keyed latest results, fields, timestamp availability, read-only weights, point-in-time/trading evaluation, grading, daily close windows and affected-company links are outside source fact discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - A2.2 A daily judgment is `Date → EXPLAINED_BY → DriverUpdate`, keyed by Date + affected Company ID + DriverUpdate ID + `llm_producer`. Separate facts and producers keep separate links; repeated claims from different sources are allowed.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Judgments, keyed latest results, fields, timestamp availability, read-only weights, point-in-time/trading evaluation, grading, daily close windows and affected-company links are outside source fact discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - A2.3 A verdict has three independent parts:
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Judgments, keyed latest results, fields, timestamp availability, read-only weights, point-in-time/trading evaluation, grading, daily close windows and affected-company links are outside source fact discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - A2.4 Reads may work out a share (weightage ÷ total weightage, within one Date + affected company + producer) and a signed force (weightage × direction). These are never stored as true causal shares, and a move may be partly unexplained. If every weight is empty, both are empty; never divide by zero or invent a weight. Do not treat link counts or summed weights as independent trading support.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Judgments, keyed latest results, fields, timestamp availability, read-only weights, point-in-time/trading evaluation, grading, daily close windows and affected-company links are outside source fact discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - A2.5 Historical explanations may use observed returns and later evidence, but predictions must use only information available at the decision time, and later explanations must never be presented as earlier predictions.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Judgments, keyed latest results, fields, timestamp availability, read-only weights, point-in-time/trading evaluation, grading, daily close windows and affected-company links are outside source fact discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - A2.6 Grade verdicts as a set: the net direction and size, plus relative ranking. Never grade a "true share" per Driver, because reality gives only one net return. An explanation is a judgment, not proven causation; no link means no recorded explanation, not no effect. Evaluate trading usefulness using decisions recorded before their outcomes, including unsuccessful signals and quiet days; explanations collected only after large moves are insufficient.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Judgments, keyed latest results, fields, timestamp availability, read-only weights, point-in-time/trading evaluation, grading, daily close windows and affected-company links are outside source fact discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - A2.7 **Daily target:** use the existing Date at the end of the previous trading day's regular close → this trading day's regular close. Its `HAS_PRICE` to the affected Company supplies the daily return: `round(100 * (current_close / previous_close - 1), 2)`, using the existing split-adjusted closes; add no separate after-hours return. No DailyCompanyMoveEvent is needed. Neither a filing's presence nor source ranking suppresses a supported explanation.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: Judgments, keyed latest results, fields, timestamp availability, read-only weights, point-in-time/trading evaluation, grading, daily close windows and affected-company links are outside source fact discovery.

numbered_rule_coverage.source_heading: - A2.8 Every fact comes from a source event; news is the source for macro facts. Date is only a verdict target, never a source. A purely macro fact with no source is held.
numbered_rule_coverage.outside_this_prompt: All discovery candidates already require a whole source event; a trading Date is not evidence. Macro facts need their original news source; no-source macro holds belong to the caller.
